query: What are the main climate risks for Kenya's agricultural sector?
synthesis:
Kenya's agricultural sector is highly vulnerable to climate change because it is approximately 98% rain-fed, with 95% of farmers lacking irrigation systems [Kenya Climate Smart Agriculture Strategy 2017 - 2026](https://www.adaptation-undp.org/sites/default/files/resources/kenya_climate_smart_agriculture_strategy.pdf) [Climate change in Africa: What will it mean for agriculture and food security?](https://www.ilri.org/news/climate-change-africa-what-will-it-mean-agriculture-and-food-security). The primary climate risks include:

*   **Increasing Temperatures and Heat Stress:** Historical records show a steady temperature increase of 0.21�C per decade since the 1960s, with projections suggesting a total increase of 2.3�C by 2050 [Climate Risk Country Profile: Kenya](https://climateknowledgeportal.worldbank.org/sites/default/files/country-profiles/15724-WB_Kenya%20Country%20Profile-WEB.pdf). These rising temperatures cause water stress for crops and extreme heat stress for livestock, which can make large areas unsuitable for production by the end of the century [Climate change in Africa: What will it mean for agriculture and food security?](https://www.ilri.org/news/climate-change-africa-what-will-it-mean-agriculture-and-food-security).
*   **Changes in Precipitation Patterns:** While northern regions have become wetter, southern agricultural areas have become drier since the 1960s [Climate Risk Country Profile: Kenya](https://climateknowledgeportal.worldbank.org/sites/default/files/country-profiles/15724-WB_Kenya%20Country%20Profile-WEB.pdf). Increased variability and decreased predictability of rainfall patterns disrupt planting cycles; specifically, high temperatures during planting can destroy crop growth [Climate Change and Food Security in Kenya](https://www.efdinitiative.org/sites/default/files/publications/drb_15-05_dec_2015_revised_jan_18_2016_0.pdf).
*   **Extreme Weather Events and Cyclical Disasters:** Kenya faces a rising frequency of droughts and floods. Since 1999, poor rainy seasons have occurred every 2 to 3 years, compared to every 5 to 6 years previously [Climate change in Africa: What will it mean for agriculture and food security?](https://www.ilri.org/news/climate-change-africa-what-will-it-mean-agriculture-and-food-security). A particular risk in drylands is the "floods after drought" pattern, where heavy precipitation follows prolonged dry spells, creating unique resilience challenges for agro-pastoralists [Frontiers | Floods after drought: storytelling with agro-pastoralists in a Kenyan dryland](https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/water/articles/10.3389/frwa.2025.1524554/full).
*   **Water Insecurity and Glacial Retreat:** Mount Kenya's glaciers, which provide water for over 2 million people, are retreating rapidly. The Lewis Glacier has shrunk by 90% since the 1930s and may disappear by 2030, threatening the water supply for surrounding agricultural landscapes [Climate change in Africa: What will it mean for agriculture and food security?](https://www.ilri.org/news/climate-change-africa-what-will-it-mean-agriculture-and-food-security).
*   **Staple Crop and Fisheries Vulnerability:** Yields from rain-fed agriculture could fall by as much as 50% in parts of sub-Saharan Africa [Climate Change and Food Security in Kenya](https://www.efdinitiative.org/sites/default/files/publications/drb_15-05_dec_2015_revised_jan_18_2016_0.pdf). Maize insecurity is projected to increase by 8.56% to 21% by 2100, while a 3�C warming scenario could make all present-day cropping areas for maize, millet, and sorghum unsuitable [Climate change in Africa: What will it mean for agriculture and food security?](https://www.ilri.org/news/climate-change-africa-what-will-it-mean-agriculture-and-food-security). Additionally, fisheries are threatened by water acidification and changing temperatures [Kenya Climate Smart Agriculture Strategy 2017 - 2026](https://www.adaptation-undp.org/sites/default/files/resources/kenya_climate_smart_agriculture_strategy.pdf).
*   **Environmental Degradation:** Climate impacts are exacerbated by soil erosion, desertification, salinization of water supplies, and deforestation [Kenya Climate Smart Agriculture Strategy 2017-2026](https://climate-laws.org/document/kenya-climate-smart-agriculture-strategy-2017-2026_bd2e) [Climate Change and Food Security in Kenya](https://www.efdinitiative.org/sites/default/files/publications/drb_15-05_dec_2015_revised_jan_18_2016_0.pdf).
